sections.content:
Population change in North West Leicestershire in 2032

The population in North West Leicestershire is projected to increase from 107,666 people in 2022 to 124,628 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 16,817 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in North West Leicestershire
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In North West Leicestershire, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 465, with 10,856 births and 11,321 deaths in North West Leicestershire between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in North West Leicestershire by 0.4%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 16,817, with 75,139 people moving to the area and 58,322 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in North West Leicestershire by 15.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 402, with 1,354 people moving to the area and 1,756 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in North West Leicestershire by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 840, with 2,783 people moving to the area and 1,943 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in North West Leicestershire by 0.8%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in North West Leicestershire in 2032

The median age in North West Leicestershire is projected to rise from 42 years in 2022 to 43 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 20% of the population in North West Leicestershire are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 19% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in North West Leicestershire between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in North West Leicestershire is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to stay around the same, at 297 in 2032 compared with 299 in 2022.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in North West Leicestershire?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in North West Leicestershire between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
